UPDATE: Ibogaine Killer

By: Laura Byrne | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
After seven years, Dr Anwar Jeewa is brought to justice.

Unique Selling Point:
In 2019, we told the story of Dr Anwar Jeewa, a dentist running a rehab clinic in Durban. Jeewa dosed his patients with ibogaine, a controversial psychedelic substance that treats the symptoms of opiate withdrawal and reportedly treats addiction. But in 2017, a young Canadian man who came to Dr Jeewa for help with his prescription addiction died just hours after arriving at the clinic. Since then, Milos Martinovic's family has been desperately hoping for justice. Now, seven years later, Jeewa has been convicted of culpable homicide and five other charges.

Script:


VOICEOVER: In 2017, a tragic death took place at a drug rehabilitation centre in Durban.
Desperate to overcome his prescription drug addiction, 26 year-old Canadian, Milos Martinovic, sought help from Dr Anwar Jeewa, a dentist offering a controversial treatment.
UPSOUND: CARTE BLANCHE ARCHIVE: We’ve done over 2500 clients already, very very safely.
VOICEOVER: Ibogaine: derived from a shrub found in Gabon, it reportedly blocks the symptoms of opiate withdrawal. But there are risks. Dr Deborah Mash is an expert in its use.
UPSOUND: CARTE BLANCHE ARCHIVE: Ibogaine has a very narrow therapeutic to toxic margin.
VOICEOVER: Jeewa gave Milos ibogaine for his opiate addiction. But he allowed him to continue self-medicating with benzodiazepine, a depressant that, among other things, relieves anxiety.
Six hours later, Milos’s heart stopped.
UPSOUND: CARTE BLANCHE ARCHIVE: We have done nothing wrong. I told him I can treat your opiate but I can’t treat your benzo.
Devi: He came here because he had an addiction. You leave him with the benzo and he ODs on the benzo while he’s on Ibogaine.
Jeewa: Ja so? So what is wrong with that, Devi?
Devi: I’ll tell you what is wrong, he’s dead.
UPSOUND: CARTE BLANCHE ARCHIVE: If this young man was already at risk for a toxic interaction – and then you’re giving more ibogaine over that time – that caused the death.
VOICEOVER: Dr Jeewa was charged with murder, four contraventions of the Medicines and Related Substances Act, and one contravention of the Prevention and Treatment of Substance Abuse Act.
Milos’s fiancé, Brooke Rombough, and his father Miki, were determined to see Jeewa held accountable.
UPSOUND: CARTE BLANCHE ARCHIVE: If he does not see imprisonment, then there is something wrong with the South African law, and something big.
VOICEOVER: The trial finally got underway in April this year.
UPSOUND: MARIUS BOOYSEN: It's the first investigation of this nature in the history of South Africa. It was a very complicated investigation and a very complicated trial. A lot of research needed to be done about ibogaine. We also had to wait very long for the toxicology reports.
VOICEOVER: Marius Booysen is a private investigator employed by Milos’s family.
UPSOUND: MARIUS BOOYSEN: We often criticize the police, but I can tell you the Hawks had really outdone themselves here. The investigation was really a marvellous job. And the state's advocate was really, really professional.
VOICEOVER: Jeewa pleaded guilty to manufacturing, selling, administering and exporting Ibogaine. He agreed to speak to us via video call.
UPSOUND: ANWAR JEEWA: I was guilty for few of the supplementary charges and not guilty for one or two, but I've accepted all because if we make the trial go much smoother and faster.
VOICEOVER: He was found guilty of running an unregistered centre – for which he says the Department of Social Development also bears responsibility.
UPSOUND: ANWAR JEEWA: Because I've been engaging with the department for 15 years and not once the Department asked me to close down.
VOICEOVER: Although Jeewa was found not guilty of murder, the court did convict him of culpable homicide.
UPSOUND: ANWAR JEEWA: Look, I was found guilty of negligence. It was not relating to the cause of death, but it was relating to us not having a proper resus unit in place to revive the patient. And I do accept the responsibility for that shortcoming. I've proven to the court that the benzodiazepine that allowed him to keep was not contraindicated with the ibogaine treatment.
UPSOUND: MARIUS BOOYSEN: The fact that Anwar Jeewa didn't have an emergency plan in place. He didn't plan properly before he started administering the ibogaine. He didn't ascertain what already did the patient have in his system and that ultimately led to his death. And the court found that he was negligent and responsible for the death. But the judge found that he didn't have the intent to kill.
VOICEOVER: Jeewa has been sentenced to three years’ correctional supervision, and fined R60 000. He must do 25 hours’ dentistry community service every month.
UPSOUND: ANWAR JEEWA: The sentence had been pretty tough, pretty harsh. But I mean, I do accept it because obviously, you know the family would be more comfortable if I was incarcerated or, you know, locked up. And I'm willing to take the punishment.
VOICEOVER: Milos’s family declined to comment, but in a victim impact statement, his fiancé Brooke wrote that she’s struggling financially, both she and their daughter still traumatised by his loss.
UPSOUND: ANWAR JEEWA: Look, I mean if if if I have lost a a loved one in similar circumstances I would also want the individual responsible to have the most harshest sentence possible. And I sincerely and publicly apologise to the family.
VOICEOVER: Jeewa says he does intend to continue manufacturing ibogaine in future, but he will do it legally.
UPSOUND: MARIUS BOOYSEN: A lot of people are asking the question, is there a future for ibogaine? I simply don't know. A lot more research needs to be done. But what I can tell you, ibogaine in the hands of unqualified individual is dangerous. It kills you. Rehabilitation owners, their staff and medical team needs to understand people that book into the centres are desperate, but they are responsible for their well-being, their medical needs and if something goes wrong, they will be held accountable.
